scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for isoproturon, technical, which is used as an active ingredient in the formulation of agricultural herbicides (primarily targeting grass weeds in wheat and barley crops).

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary/Mandatory under the Insecticides Act. Manufacturers are encouraged to apply for the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) to print on product containers as a certified assurance of quality. Additionally, all packaging, labeling, and distribution of technical-grade isoproturon must strictly comply with statutory registrations and warning declarations mandated under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder.

requirements.detail: Mandates that all tests must be carried out as referred to in column (4) of Table 1.

Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water conforming to IS 1070 must be employed in all analytical tests. Pure chemicals must not contain impurities that affect the results of analysis.

Isoproturon is hydrolysed using potassium hydroxide in aqueous diethylene glycol (1 : 1 by volume). Dimethylamine, the volatile product of hydrolysis, is distilled off and absorbed in standard hydrochloric acid. From the quantity of acid consumed by dimethylamine, the percentage of isoproturon present in the original sample is computed.
Requires a high-precision, all-glass distillation assembly of a suitable type as illustrated in Fig. 1.

The estimation procedure mandates five specific chemical reagents: a) 0.2 N Hydrochloric Acid Solution; b) 0.2 N Sodium Hydroxide Solution; c) 35 percent aqueous Potassium Hydroxide Solution; d) Diethylene Glycol; and e) Silicon Defoamer.

Accurately weighs 1.0 g ± 0.1 g of the isoproturon, technical sample and transfers it to the reaction flask. Adds 50 ml of diethylene glycol, one or two boiling chips, and 1 ml of silicon defoamer to check foaming. In a receiver beaker, 50 ml of hydrochloric acid (0.2 N) is taken, in which the delivery tube end dips. Adds 50 ml of potassium hydroxide (35 percent) solution to the flask through a dropping funnel, closes the stop-cock, and heats the contents to boiling.

Distillation is continued for up to approximately 24 hours. The distillation can be stopped when the contents of the flask turn orange-brown, confirming the distillate has ceased to be alkaline. This neutral endpoint must be verified using multi-range pH paper, indicating a pH of exactly 7.

Requires back-titrating the excess hydrochloric acid in the receiver beaker against 0.2 N sodium hydroxide to calculate active isoproturon content via: Isoproturon (Percent) = [(V1 * N1) - (V2 * N2)] * 20.6 / M, where V1 = volume of HCl originally taken, N1 = normality of HCl, V2 = volume of NaOH consumed, N2 = normality of NaOH, and M = mass in g of the sample.

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing active ingredient content, moisture, or impurities must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12004 : 2026 is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical requirements, packaging guidelines, and testing protocols for isoproturon, technical. Finalized by the FAD 01 Pesticides Sectional Committee, this standard regulates the chemical quality of this active substituted-urea herbicide, which is widely utilized in agriculture to control grass weeds in cereal crops. It mandates conducting all tests using pure reagents and distilled water conforming to IS 1070. It outlines a detailed alkaline hydrolysis method—using diethylene glycol and potassium hydroxide to distill off volatile dimethylamine into standard hydrochloric acid, followed by back-titration against sodium hydroxide—to calculate the exact active percentage of isoproturon, ensuring product potency and statutory safety under the Insecticides Act, 1968.
